vagueSymptom: After I open and close Quick View several times, the tab gets heavier and sluggish; closing the modal does not seem to give the memory back.
plantedCondition: The runtime widget-preferences response returns a different channel key for each read, so destroy removes no listener registered under the earlier key.

requiredDiagnosisFacts.fact: The post-interaction heap snapshot retains additional objects after six Quick View open/close cycles while the baseline does not.
requiredDiagnosisFacts.why: A before/after heap comparison establishes retained growth rather than process-memory noise.

requiredDiagnosisFacts.fact: At least six detached review-frame document roots remain after the faulty run, while the healthy control retains none.
requiredDiagnosisFacts.why: The detached frame/document population identifies the removed modal content as the retained population.

requiredDiagnosisFacts.fact: A surviving message listener retains each removed review-frame document and its parsed review payload.
requiredDiagnosisFacts.why: The retaining path distinguishes JavaScript retention from decoded images or ordinary browser cache growth.

requiredDiagnosisFacts.fact: Listener removal did not match the channel key used for registration, so destroy silently left each listener installed.
requiredDiagnosisFacts.why: This is the concrete lifecycle failure responsible for the retained frames.

requiredEvidence.evidence: Heap snapshots taken after forced GC before and after at least six open/close cycles show the detached-frame retention in the faulty variant.
requiredEvidence.why: Forced collection and the temporal comparison rule out ordinary live state.

requiredEvidence.evidence: Changing only the runtime channel-key sequence to the healthy manifest removes the detached documents entirely after forced GC.
requiredEvidence.why: The control rules out decoded image data and browser-cache growth as the explanation.

requiredEvidence.evidence: The heap retaining path passes through the surviving message-listener registry to the detached document and parsed payload.
requiredEvidence.why: Retainer attribution establishes the mechanism instead of merely observing growth.

plausibleWrongAnswer: Decoded product images or normal browser cache growth accounts for the memory increase.
